sentences.text: Lanzhousaurus was a large bipedal herbivore estimated to be about 10 meters long and weighing between 4 and 6 tons.
The only known species of this genus is Lanzhousaurus magnidens.
This species is known from a partial skeleton found in the Hekou Group.
It differs from other iguanodontids by possessing large individual teeth and a small number of them.
The mandible of Lanzhousaurus was longer than one meter, suggesting a very large size.
The animal possessed compressed metacarpals II and IV.
The neural spines on the back were moderately high, giving it a low profile at the hips.
The teeth of Lanzhousaurus reached 14 centimeters in length on a lower jaw that was 1 meter long.
These teeth are the largest discovered in a known herbivorous dinosaur.
The genus Lanzhousaurus was described by You, Ji, and Li in 2005.
Fossils of Lanzhousaurus were found in the Lanzhou Bed in Gansu province, China.
The huge teeth indicate that Lanzhousaurus was a styracosternan iguanodont.
The tooth enamel of Lanzhousaurus grew very rapidly.
Along with Lurdusaurus from Niger, Lanzhousaurus represents a previously unknown lineage of massively built quadrupedal ornithopods.
Phylogenetic analyses recovered Lanzhousaurus as a non-hadrosauriform styracosternan member of the Ankylopollexia.
The parent group of Lanzhousaurus is Styracosterna.
Lanzhousaurus lived in the Gansu region of China during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian).
Lanzhousaurus lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, approximately 135 million years ago, during the Valanginian.
Lanzhousaurus lived in what is now Asia.
The time range for Lanzhousaurus is from the Barremian to the Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago).
This discovery implies a close connection between Eurasia and Africa during the Early Cretaceous.
